meta.environment: Personal instance https://svcdemoaz.puremonitor.supercom.com/AQApplication/Neil/ — Chromium 1228 (Playwright 1.61), Windows 11, browser timezone Asia/Jerusalem

severityScale.Critical: Wrong or lost safety-relevant data, silent corruption, or the console becomes unusable. No workaround.
severityScale.High: A PRD requirement is broken for a main flow; workaround is awkward or unreliable.
severityScale.Medium: Requirement broken in a secondary flow, or a workaround exists.

priorityScale.P2: Fix in this release if possible; release blocker only in combination.
priorityScale.P3: Can be scheduled for a later release.

bugs.title: Pager hides the last (partial) page: totalPages is floor(total/pageSize) instead of ceiling
steps: Open the console with the 11 seeded offenders.
Click Next ›, then try to click Next › again.
bugs.expected: 3 pages (ceil(11/5)); page 3 shows "Peretz, Michael"; every one of the 11 offenders is reachable.
bugs.actual: Pager shows 2 pages and Next is disabled on page 2. "Peretz, Michael" (11th alphabetically) can never be reached by paging. The API itself returns him on page=3, while reporting totalPages=2.
bugs.layerAnalysis: API. The UI renders `totalPages` exactly as the API returns it and disables Next when page >= totalPages. The API response is internally inconsistent: total=11, pageSize=5, totalPages=2, yet page=3 returns one item. Same floor() pattern for every size: pageSize=3 → 3 (expected 4), pageSize=4 → 2 (expected 3), pageSize=10 → 1 (expected 2).
bugs.impact: Any offender who sorts onto the final partial page is invisible when browsing the roster. With 11 records that is 1 offender; it grows to up to 4 per page size.

bugs.title: Deleting an offender leaves their trail points in the system and in the trail-point total
steps: DELETE /api/offenders/X (204), or delete through the UI.
bugs.expected: Trail of X is gone (404 or empty) and totalLocationPoints = N − 3. The top bar "Trail points" decreases by 3.
bugs.actual: GET /api/offenders/X/trail still returns all 3 points. totalLocationPoints stays at N. The top bar keeps counting them.
bugs.layerAnalysis: API / data. The delete endpoint removes the offender row only; location rows are not cascaded. /api/stats counts the orphaned rows. The UI is correct — it re-reads /api/stats after delete and shows what it receives. Evidence of accumulation on the Neil instance: 11 offenders own 166 points, but stats reports 186 (orphans from earlier deletes).
bugs.impact: Location history of a removed person is retained (privacy/data-retention risk) and the dashboard total is permanently inflated.

bugs.title: Saving the Edit form silently resets the offender's Risk level to "Low"
steps: Create or pick an offender with Risk level = High (e.g. Cohen, David).
Click Edit. The form shows Risk level = High.
Change only the first name (or change Risk level to Medium) and click Save.
Look at the Risk badge in the list, and GET /api/offenders/{id}.
bugs.expected: Risk level keeps the value shown in the form (High, or Medium if changed).
bugs.actual: Risk level is saved as Low in every case — whatever the form shows.
bugs.layerAnalysis: UI: the Save handler builds the PUT body from firstName, lastName, nationalId, dateOfBirth and status only — riskLevel is never sent (visible in the request payload in DevTools/Playwright). API (contributing): PUT treats a missing riskLevel as the default "Low" instead of rejecting the request (400) or keeping the stored value. Proof: PUT with riskLevel=High persists High; the same PUT without riskLevel stores Low.
bugs.evidence:
UI request body on Save: {"firstName":"Zedd","lastName":"Aaqa","nationalId":"911000001","dateOfBirth":"1980-05-05","status":"Active"}   ← no riskLevel
GET api/offenders/132 after Save → "riskLevel":"Low" (was "High")
Direct API: PUT {…,"riskLevel":"High"} → High ; PUT {…without riskLevel} → Low
bugs.impact: Any routine edit (typo in a name) downgrades a High-risk offender to Low with no warning. Monitoring priority is driven by this field.

bugs.title: Date of birth is displayed one month too early (January shows as month "00")
steps: Compare the Date of birth column with GET /api/offenders.
Select an offender and compare the DOB in the detail header.
bugs.expected: Cohen, David → 07/03/1982; Mizrahi, Rachel → 12/01/1988 (DD/MM/YYYY of the stored value).
bugs.actual: Cohen → 07/02/1982; Mizrahi → 12/00/1988. Every DOB is shifted back one month, in the list and in the detail header.
bugs.layerAnalysis: UI. The API returns the correct ISO dates ("1982-03-07", "1988-01-12") and the Edit form pre-fills the correct value (1982-03-07), so storage is right. The display formatter uses JavaScript's 0-based Date.getMonth() without +1. Secondary issue in the same function: the date is parsed as UTC midnight and read in local time, so for operators west of UTC (e.g. America/New_York) the day is also one less.
bugs.evidence:
API: {"lastName":"Mizrahi","dateOfBirth":"1988-01-12"}
UI list row: "Mizrahi, Rachel | 204518793 | 12/00/1988"
UI detail: "DOB: 07/02/1982" for Cohen (API 1982-03-07)
Same row, two browser timezones (API 1998-02-06): Asia/Jerusalem → "Amar, Noa | 06/01/1998"; America/New_York → "Amar, Noa | 05/01/1998"
bugs.impact: Operators verify identity by DOB; every displayed DOB is wrong and January dates are impossible values.

bugs.title: "Latest reading" shows the speed, battery and signal of the OLDEST trail point
steps: GET /api/offenders/1/trail and find the point with the latest timestamp (2026-08-09T11:29Z, id 1).
bugs.expected: 23 km/h · 68% battery · 1/5 signal · Last seen 09/08/2026 14:29 (all from the newest point).
bugs.actual: 38.4 km/h · 87% battery · 4/5 signal (values of the OLDEST point, 06:22Z) next to "Last seen 09/08/2026, 14:29" (newest). The card mixes two different points.
bugs.layerAnalysis: UI. The API data is complete and the UI already sorts the trail chronologically for this card; it then takes element [0] (oldest) for the readings and the last element for "Last seen". Independent of BUG-06: it reproduces with a trail inserted in perfect chronological order.
bugs.evidence:
Trail (API) newest point id 1 @ 11:29Z: speed 23, battery 68, signal 1
UI card: "38.4 km/h · 87% battery · 4/5 signal · Last seen: 09/08/2026, 14:29"
bugs.impact: The operator sees a healthy battery/signal while the device is actually at 68% / 1 bar — low-battery and lost-signal situations are hidden.

bugs.title: Trail is returned and drawn in insertion order, not chronological order
steps: Select Cohen, David in the console; read the trail table and look at the red line on the map.
bugs.expected: Points ordered oldest → newest in the API, in the table and along the map line.
bugs.actual: API returns points ordered by id (timestamps 11:29, 07:10, 10:21, 06:44 …). The table lists them in the same order and the map line zig-zags between them instead of following the movement. Reproduces for all 11 seeded offenders.
bugs.layerAnalysis: API: the order violates API-04 directly (sorted by id, not timestamp). UI: also at fault for FR-07 — it already sorts a copy for the Latest-reading card but uses the unsorted array for the table and the polyline, so even a fixed API would leave the UI relying on server order.
bugs.impact: The map no longer shows the real route; an operator cannot reconstruct where the person went or in what order.

bugs.title: Search is case-sensitive ("cohen" finds nothing)
bugs.expected: Cohen, David is returned (matching is case-insensitive).
bugs.actual: "No offenders found" / API total 0. "Cohen" returns 1. Substring matching itself works ("ohe" → Cohen).
bugs.layerAnalysis: API. The UI passes the typed text unchanged as ?search=; the API returns 0 for the lowercase term and 1 for the capitalised one.
bugs.evidence:
GET api/offenders?search=Cohen → total 1
GET api/offenders?search=cohen → total 0
GET api/offenders?search=COHEN → total 0
bugs.impact: Operators who type in lower case conclude an offender does not exist.

bugs.title: Unknown offender id returns 200 (empty body / empty trail) instead of 404
bugs.actual: GET offender → 200 with an empty body. GET trail → 200 []. A deleted offender id also returns 200 (empty). PUT/DELETE/POST-location on the same id correctly return 404, so the API is inconsistent.
bugs.layerAnalysis: API — pure contract issue, no UI involved.
bugs.impact: Clients cannot tell "not found" from "found"; a JSON parse of the empty body fails in consumers.

bugs.title: Duplicate national ID is accepted on create
steps: In the UI click + Add Offender, enter national ID 305412876 (already used by Cohen, David) and valid other fields, click Create — or POST the same payload to /api/offenders.
bugs.expected: 400 with an error such as "National ID already exists"; nothing saved.
bugs.actual: 201 Created; two offenders now share national ID 305412876. Searching that ID returns both.
bugs.layerAnalysis: API — the uniqueness rule is not enforced server-side (the UI has no client-side check either, but the PRD rule is a data-integrity rule that must live in the API).
bugs.impact: Two people with one identity: trails, alerts and court records can be attributed to the wrong person.

bugs.title: Required fields Last name and National ID are not enforced
steps: (UI) Add Offender, fill only First name, click Create.
bugs.expected: 400 "Last name is required." / "National ID is required."; nothing saved.
bugs.actual: 201 Created for both. The UI creates an offender displayed as ", NoLast" that sorts to the top of the list. Only firstName is validated.
bugs.layerAnalysis: API — firstName validation exists and works (400 "First name is required."), proving the validator is present but incomplete.
bugs.impact: Incomplete identity records; nameless rows in the roster.

bugs.title: Date of birth is not validated: future dates and non-dates are accepted
bugs.expected: 400 for both (DOB must be a valid date in the past).
bugs.actual: 201 for both; "notadate" is stored verbatim and rendered as "notadate" in the DOB column.
bugs.layerAnalysis: API — no date parsing or range check; field is stored as free text.
bugs.impact: Invalid identity data; downstream age calculations break.

bugs.title: Risk level and Status accept any string (e.g. "Critical", "Deleted")
bugs.expected: 400 — allowed values are Low/Medium/High and Active/Inactive.
bugs.actual: 201 for both; values stored and shown as unstyled badges. PUT accepts them too ("Extreme").
bugs.layerAnalysis: API — no enum validation. The UI only offers valid options, so this is reachable via API (and any integration) only.
bugs.impact: Offenders with an unknown risk/status fall out of any filter, report or count based on the defined values.

bugs.title: PUT /api/offenders/{id} performs no validation at all
steps: PUT with nationalId of another offender (305412876).
bugs.expected: 400 with error description for each (same rules as create, API-03).
bugs.actual: 200 for every request and the invalid values are stored — even an empty first name, which POST correctly rejects.
bugs.layerAnalysis: API — the create validator is not applied to update.
bugs.impact: Every create-time rule can be bypassed by creating a valid record and editing it.

bugs.title: Location points are not validated: invalid coordinates, negative speed, battery and signal out of range all accepted
steps: POST /api/offenders/{id}/locations with each of: lat 91, lat -91, lon 181, lon -181, speedKmh -1, batteryPct -1, batteryPct 101, signal 0, signal 6, timestamp "garbage", and an empty body {}.
(UI) Select an offender → + Add location → speed -5, battery 150 → Add.
bugs.expected: 400 with an error description for every invalid value; nothing saved.
bugs.actual: 201 {"ok":true} for every one; values stored as sent. {} creates a point at 0,0 with signal 0. The UI form adds the -5 km/h / 150% point to the table.
bugs.layerAnalysis: API — no validation on the endpoint. The UI has no client-side checks either, but API-03 requires the server to enforce the rules.
bugs.evidence:
POST {lat:91,…} → 201 {"ok":true}
POST {batteryPct:101,…} → 201
POST {signal:6,…} → 201
POST {} → 201 (stored lat 0, lon 0, signal 0)
UI trail row after form submit: "32.10000 | 34.80000 | -5 km/h | 150% | 4/5"
bugs.impact: Corrupt telemetry is stored and displayed as real; it also triggers BUG-15 (console crash).

bugs.title: A trail point with signal outside 1–5 crashes the whole console to a blank page
steps: Create an offender and POST a location with signal 6 (accepted, see BUG-14).
Open the console, search the offender and click the row.
bugs.expected: Trail renders; the bad value is shown or flagged, the rest of the console keeps working.
bugs.actual: The entire page goes blank (React root unmounted). Browser console: "RangeError: Invalid count value: -1". A reload brings the list back, but selecting that offender crashes it again.
bugs.layerAnalysis: UI. The popup text is built with "▮".repeat(signal) + "▯".repeat(5 − signal); for signal > 5 (or < 0) repeat() throws, inside a React effect, with no error boundary. The API returns the data correctly — the UI cannot render it. BUG-14 is what lets such data in, but the UI must not crash on unexpected data.
bugs.evidence:
pageerror: "Invalid count value: -1"
#root innerHTML length after click: 0 (blank page)
bugs.impact: One malformed reading from a device makes the monitoring console unusable for that offender, with no message to the operator.

bugs.title: Add-location form fails silently when the server rejects the point
steps: Leave Latitude and Longitude empty, click Add.
bugs.expected: A clear error message (e.g. "Latitude is required"); the form stays open.
bugs.actual: Nothing visible happens. The API answers 400; the UI throws an unhandled promise rejection ("Request failed (400)") and shows no message.
bugs.layerAnalysis: UI. The add-location submit handler awaits the request without try/catch, unlike create/edit which show the error banner. (The empty-body 400 from the API is BUG-18.)
bugs.evidence:
pageerror: "Request failed (400)"
No .banner.error element; form still open, unchanged
bugs.impact: The operator believes the point was saved, or does not know why it was not.

bugs.title: Blank Speed / Battery in the add-location form are silently saved as 0
steps: Enter only Latitude 32.2 and Longitude 34.9, leave Speed and Battery empty, click Add.
bugs.expected: Rejected with a message (no value is not the same as 0).
bugs.actual: A point with 0 km/h and 0% battery is added. Same for an empty Signal (→ 0, outside 1–5).
bugs.layerAnalysis: UI. The form converts empty input with parseFloat(x) || 0 and parseInt(x) || 0 before sending, so the API receives explicit zeros.
bugs.evidence: UI trail row after submit: "32.20000 | 34.90000 | 0 km/h | 0% | 3/5"
bugs.impact: A fake 0% battery reading is recorded and, once BUG-05 is fixed, will show in Latest reading.

bugs.title: Malformed request body returns 400 with an empty body (no error description)
bugs.expected: 400 with a JSON error description, like the other validation errors ({"error":"…"}).
bugs.layerAnalysis: API — model-binding failures bypass the error formatter used by the validator.
bugs.evidence:
POST api/offenders  body: garbage → 400, Content-Length 0
POST api/offenders/1/locations {"lat":null} → 400, empty body
bugs.impact: Clients (including this UI, see BUG-16) can only show "Request failed (400)".
